newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power down before thermometer rises.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power down before thermometer rises.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast fell in price for Monday delivery as frigid cold was expected to give way to warmer temperatures early next week, industry sources said.
Forecasts called for temperatures in the region to continue in the 10-20 degrees Fahrenheit below normal range through to Sunday, with warmer to near-normal levels by the middle of next week.

Firm, peak power prices into the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Monday were discussed at $19.00-21.00 from next day discussion at $35.00-36.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Thursday, the brokers and marketers said.
Firm, off-peak electricity prices into TVA for Monday were assessed lower at $12.50-14.00 from near $22.00 on Thursday.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks for Monday delivery were talked at $21.50-23.50 from talk at $32.00-37.00 on Thursday.
Firm, off-peak power for Monday at the Ga./Fla. border was pegged at $15.00-16.50 from a notional assessment at $22.00-23.00 on Thursday.
